Where to record a deed in Baltimore County

Deeds for Baltimore County property go to the Land Records department of the Circuit Court for Baltimore County, inside the Clerk's Office at the County Courts Building, 401 Bosley Avenue, 2nd Floor, Towson, MD 21204. The mailing address is P.O. Box 6754, Towson, MD 21285-6754, and the office is open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Each Maryland county and Baltimore City runs its own land records department inside the circuit court clerk's office. Baltimore City records its own deeds, so a property inside the independent city is not recorded in Towson.

What the land records office can record

The office records any instrument that affects a legal interest in real property, including deeds, mortgages, liens, powers of attorney and certain leases. Clerks accept documents that meet the requirements and reject those that do not. They cannot help fill out forms or review a document before it is recorded.

That rule is the main reason sellers use a title company or attorney. A rejected deed costs days, and when a closing date is set, days matter. Talk to a lawyer before recording a new deed.

Numbers worth saving from the Clerk's Office:

  • Land Records Recording: 410-887-2651
  • Land Records Indexing: 410-887-3088
  • Main number: 410-887-2601; TTY users can dial Maryland Relay at 711
  • Foreclosure department: 410-887-2652

Taxes due before a deed is recorded

Baltimore County collects its own transfer tax and the state recordation tax before the Clerk's Office takes a deed. The county's Office of Budget and Finance handles both at a separate counter. Bring payment to the Transfer and Recordation Section at 400 Washington Avenue, Room 154, Towson, MD 21204, with checks payable to Baltimore County, Maryland.

RequirementAmount or rule
Baltimore County transfer tax1.5% of consideration
State recordation tax$2.50 per $500 (or fraction of $500) of consideration, or of the principal debt secured
Lien certificateRequired for any deed that changes or transfers ownership; a deed without one will not be processed
Maryland State Intake SheetRequired with every deed and property-related document
Counter hoursMonday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

The first $22,000 of consideration for a grantee's principal residence is exempt from the Baltimore County transfer tax. Call the Transfer Tax Section at 410-887-2416 to ask whether your deal qualifies before you count on that credit.

The contract should say which party pays each tax. Have the title company show every charge on the settlement statement.

Why a deed needs a lien certificate

The lien certificate lets the county confirm that no taxes or charges are owed on the property account before ownership changes. It costs $55, and you can apply in person or by mail with a self-addressed, stamped envelope.

Order it as soon as a contract is signed. If tax is owed, it must in most cases be paid before the transfer, which pushes a closing date if you discover a balance the day before settlement. Taxpayer Services at 410-887-2416 answers account questions.

Call before you plan a same-day pickup, since the lien certificate service can be interrupted during county system updates.

Deeds that need state assessment approval

Agricultural-use deeds and partial-transfer deeds must first be approved by the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. The Towson office is at 300 East Joppa Road, Room 602.

If you are splitting a lot, build the approval into your timeline. A partial-transfer deed sent to the Clerk's Office without it risks rejection.

  • Whole-parcel residential deed: intake sheet, lien certificate, tax payment.
  • Agricultural-use deed: the same items plus approval from the assessments department.
  • Partial-transfer deed: the same items plus approval from the assessments department.

Can you e-record a deed in Baltimore County?

Under Maryland Rule 1-322, documents cannot be filed directly by electronic transmission, though the Clerk's site links an E-Recording for Land Records page under E-Services. Some Maryland counties accept deeds and other documents through Simplifile, and electronic signatures require an Affidavit of Intent to Use Electronic Signature, form CC094.

Ask your title company whether it uses an electronic channel in Baltimore County or delivers the deed in person. Deed-related messages from the county tax office arrive from one email address under the subject line Official Tax Notice. Add that sender to your safe list so the message is not lost in spam.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Baltimore County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Recording fees, payment and copies

The Clerk's Office accepts cash, MasterCard, Visa and Discover, plus checks or money orders payable to Clerk of the Circuit Court. Personal out-of-state checks and debit cards are refused. Land records fees are set in a separate Circuit Court fee schedule, so get the current amounts from the Clerk's Office before you bring payment.

For research, the Maryland State Archives runs a free viewer for deeds at landrec.msa.maryland.gov, and an account is required. Copies from the viewer cost $0.50 per page. Land records documents can also be requested from the Clerk's Office online or by email.

Fees on a Maryland deed are split. Some go to the land records department and some to the local county finance office, which is why you make one payment at the Clerk's Office and another at the county's Transfer and Recordation Section.

Recording steps for a seller

Closing day goes smoothly when the paperwork is ready in the right order. Your title company or attorney will normally handle these steps, and knowing them helps you ask the right questions.

  • Order the lien certificate and pay any balance it reveals.
  • Complete the Maryland State Intake Sheet for the deed.
  • Pay the county transfer tax and state recordation tax at the Transfer and Recordation Section.
  • Deliver the deed and the receipts to the Land Records counter and pay the recording fee there.
  • Request a copy of the recorded deed for your files.

An as-is cash sale uses the same recording steps. What it skips is the buyer's lender, so there is no appraisal or repair list standing between you and the closing table.

Inherited Baltimore County houses

An heir selling a Baltimore County house deals with more than the land records counter. The Clerk's Office lists a Register of Wills at 410-887-6680 and the Orphans' Court at 410-887-6516. Neither can stand in for a lawyer's advice.

If taxes were left unpaid, settle them with the Office of Budget and Finance at 410-887-2404 first, because the lien certificate will show them. The county steps above apply however the house is sold, including an as-is sale.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Baltimore County Circuit Court land records office?

It is in the Clerk's Office at 401 Bosley Avenue, 2nd Floor, Towson, MD 21204, open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Land Records Recording is at 410-887-2651.

What is the Baltimore County transfer tax?

The county charges 1.5 percent of consideration. The first $22,000 of consideration for a grantee's principal residence is exempt.

What is the Maryland recordation tax on a Baltimore County deed?

The state recordation tax is $2.50 per $500, or fraction of $500, of consideration or of the debt secured. Checks go to Baltimore County, Maryland.

Do I need a lien certificate to record a deed in Baltimore County?

Yes. Any deed that changes or transfers ownership needs one, and a deed without it will not be processed. The fee is $55.

Does the Clerk's Office help me fill out a deed?

No. Clerks cannot help fill out forms or review documents before recording, so speak with a lawyer or your title company first.

Where deeds are recorded in Montgomery County

Deeds, mortgages and releases for the entire county are recorded by the Land Records department of the Montgomery County Circuit Court in Rockville, the county seat. Staff there work from separate desks, and the land records page has the numbers.

  • Recording Department, 240-777-9470: turning in documents to be recorded.
  • Public Information Room, 240-777-9477: general questions about land documents.
  • Indexing Department, 240-777-9476: grantor and grantee name indexes.
  • Duplication Department, 240-777-9480: copies and certified copies.

The Public Information Room is in the North Tower, second floor, Room 2120, open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays. Recording stops earlier, at 4:00 p.m. If you plan to carry a deed in on settlement day, build your schedule around that cutoff. Most sellers never make the trip, because the title company or settlement attorney files the deed.

Searching land records and liens for free

MDLandRec, run by the Maryland State Archives at landrec.msa.maryland.gov, costs nothing to search. A first-time user applies for a login with a valid email address, and the password usually arrives within about an hour on a business day.

You can search by name, by liber and folio, or by tax account number, and print what you find. The system covers land records, plats, liens, judgments and financing statements. For a seller it is the fastest way to learn whether an old mortgage, a judgment lien or an unreleased deed of trust still clings to the title.

Two limits to plan for: plats live on a separate site, PLATS.NET, and the county keeps no individual house location plats. Equity index books from 1777 to 1981 are held by the Maryland State Archives, not at the courthouse.

Recording fees

The statewide circuit court fee schedule, effective September 2, 2026, sets the recording fee at $60 for an instrument involving solely a principal residence. On top of that, a $40 surcharge applies to recordable instruments, continued by Chapter 538 of the 2020 legislative session.

Document or serviceFee
Instrument involving solely a principal residence$60
Other instrument, 9 pages or less$60
Other instrument, 10 pages or more$115
Release, 9 pages or less$50
Copy, per page$0.50
Certified copy$5 plus $0.50 per page
Surcharge on recordable instruments$40

The figures come from the Maryland Judiciary fee summary. Schedules change, so phone the Recording Department for the exact total on your document before settlement.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Montgomery County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Recordation tax and transfer tax

Montgomery County's recordation tax has three layers, and it grows once the price tops $500,000. Before the 2023 change, the structure was a base rate of $2.08 per $500, a school increment of $2.37 per $500, and a premium of $2.30 per $500 on the portion above $500,000.

Bill 17-23 was enacted May 9, 2023, by a 7 to 4 vote, and the new rates took effect October 1, 2023. The base and school rates did not move. Only the premium changed, and it now steps up with the price.

The premium is $5.75 per $500 on amounts from $600,000 to $750,000, $6.33 per $500 over $750,000 up to $1 million, and $6.90 per $500 over $1 million.

The one percent county transfer tax was left unchanged, and state law lets Montgomery set variable transfer tax rates by property value. For the exact figure at your price, call the county Department of Finance at 101 Monroe Street, 15th Floor, Rockville.

Tax breaks that affect who pays what

First-time homebuyers get the first $100,000 of the sale price exempted from the base recordation rate. The first $100,000 of value is also untaxed for a home that the buyer occupies at least seven months in its first year. That $100,000 exemption does not extend to refinancing, second homes or commercial deals.

The legal basis is Maryland's recordation law, which allows each county to exempt a set amount for owner-occupied homes. As a seller you will feel this at the settlement table. These breaks change what the buyer owes, and they interact with the Maryland default rule on dividing closing taxes. Ask your settlement attorney to show the split on the draft closing statement, and compare it with what your sale contract says about who pays. Raise any mismatch before settlement day, not at the table.

The Montgomery County housing market in brief

Montgomery County is the most populous county in Maryland, with 1,062,061 residents in the 2020 census. Housing is mostly owner-occupied: 419,402 housing units as of July 1, 2025, 389,210 households for 2020 to 2024, and an owner-occupied rate of 65.3%. Median gross rent is $2,068, and median monthly owner costs with a mortgage are $2,929. About 88.1% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so most buyers and sellers are local movers, and every deed goes to the same Rockville land records office.

What to bring to the recording step

The title company or settlement attorney normally handles recording, but you should still know what goes in the packet.

  • The signed deed, with the exemption claim written out if the transfer is exempt from tax.
  • The recordation and transfer tax amounts due on the deed.
  • Releases for any mortgage being paid off, recorded at the $50 release fee for documents of 9 pages or less.

Here is how a typical sale moves through the office. At settlement, you sign the deed and the closing agent collects the taxes and fees. The agent then delivers the package to the Recording Department before the 4:00 p.m. cutoff, and the payoff lender's release is recorded so the old mortgage comes off the record. Ask the closing agent for a copy of the recorded deed and the receipt for the taxes paid, and file both with your sale papers. Once the deed is indexed, the sale shows up in a land records search under your name as grantor and the buyer's as grantee.

The land records page also posts notices about transfer-on-death deeds and notices of death filings. An heir selling a parent's house should check whether one was recorded. If you want to sell without repairs or showings, a cash buyer such as Cash Home Buyers can close on your timeline and let the settlement company deal with the recording paperwork.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I record a deed in Montgomery County, Maryland?

Deeds are recorded by the Land Records department of the Montgomery County Circuit Court in Rockville. Reach the Recording Department at 240-777-9470, and note that recording ends at 4:00 p.m.

How much does it cost to record a Montgomery County deed?

The fee schedule effective September 2, 2026 lists $60 for an instrument involving solely a principal residence, plus the $40 surcharge on recordable instruments, before recordation and transfer taxes. Call the Recording Department to confirm the total for your document.

Did Montgomery County raise its recordation tax?

Yes. Bill 17-23, enacted May 9, 2023, raised the premium rate on amounts above $600,000 starting October 1, 2023. The base and school rates stayed the same.

Can I search Montgomery County land records online?

Yes. MDLandRec at landrec.msa.maryland.gov is free once you register with an email address. You can search by name, liber and folio, or tax account number.

Who pays the recordation and transfer tax on a sale?

Maryland presumes the buyer and seller split them equally unless the contract or law says otherwise. For a first-time buyer who will occupy the home, the seller pays them unless the parties expressly agree otherwise.

Where to record a deed in Prince George's County

Recording takes two stops in person. The county Office of Finance in Largo comes first, then the Land Records Division of the Circuit Court in Upper Marlboro. The Finance step has to be done before the court will take the deed.

  • Step 1, Office of Finance: 1301 McCormick Drive, Suite 1100, Largo; 301-952-4030; 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. weekdays.
  • Step 2, Land Records Division: 14701 Governor Oden Bowie Drive, Room J1108, Upper Marlboro; 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. weekdays.

Bring the original deed, one full copy, and the State of Maryland land instrument intake sheet. A deed that claims an exemption from recording fees or state transfer tax has to cite every applicable code section from the Maryland Annotated Code. The Land Records Division answers at 301-780-2253, and the courthouse main line is 301-952-3655.

Recording fees

An instrument of 1 to 9 pages costs $20, and that fee covers every page when the instrument concerns a principal residence. A $40 surcharge sits on top for recorded documents. For the current amount, call the Land Records Division at 301-780-2253 before you record.

Clerk's recording and copy fees
ServiceFee
Other instrument, 1 to 9 pages (all pages if principal residence)$20
Other instrument, 10 or more pages, not a principal residence$75
Release, 1 to 9 pages$10
Surcharge on recorded documents (not powers of attorney, plats, chattel)$40
Copy of a deed or other document$2
Copy of a deed of trust or mortgage$5
Certified copy of a deed of trust or mortgage$10
Certified copy, other instruments$7

Payment is due when the document is recorded. The office takes cash, checks, money orders and credit cards, with checks and money orders payable to The Clerk of the Circuit Court. Documents come back by mail when you supply a return address, and otherwise they wait for pickup.

Transfer and recordation taxes

Three taxes can apply to a sale. The county transfer tax is 1.4%, set under County Code sections 10-187 and 10-188. The state recordation tax is $5.50 per $1,000 of consideration, and the county's Finance Affidavit instructions express the same figure as $2.75 per $500, rounded up to the next $500. The state transfer tax is 0.5%, or 0.25% for a qualifying first-time buyer, under Tax-Property 13-203.

Questions about the state transfer tax go to the Land Records Division. Questions about county transfer and recordation tax go to the Office of Finance. Because the county transfer tax alone is a sizable line item, settle in the contract who pays it. Maryland's default is an equal split unless the contract or a law says otherwise.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Prince George's County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The Finance Affidavit

The Finance Affidavit is the form Prince George's County uses to claim an exemption from the county transfer tax or the state recordation tax. Every instrument recorded in the county's land records is taxable unless Maryland's code or the county code exempts it, and the affidavit is how a filer names the exemption.

Most of its clauses concern loans and refinances:

  • Clause A: a principal residence refinance, where recordation tax applies to the difference between the new loan and the unpaid principal balance.
  • Clause B-1: a principal residence with a purchase money deed of trust recorded for more than 12 months, covering new loans, modifications and home equity lines.
  • Clause B-2: a refinance by a borrower who does not qualify for B-1, paired with Clause A.
  • Clause C: a refinance of a non-principal residence or investment property, where the 1.4% county transfer tax applies to the difference between the new and original loan amounts.

The property must be the borrower's principal residence in state assessment records. Call the county Treasury for submission details.

Disclosures Maryland requires for Prince George's County sales

Prince George's County has its own line items in the state's residential contract statute. Section 14-117 of the Real Property Article requires, where deferred private water and sewer assessments are recorded, that the contract disclose eight items, including the assessment amount, remaining payments, interest rate, payoff amount, and that prepayment carries no penalty. Those assessments cannot be amortized over more than 20 years.

The contract must also disclose whether a development impact fee was imposed on the property, the total amount, and any unpaid balance. Statewide, every residential sale needs a homestead property tax credit statement, and one- or two-unit contracts need the statement that recordation and transfer taxes are shared equally unless negotiated otherwise.

Property tax and tax sale facts for sellers

The county real property rate is $1.0000 per $100 of assessed value for fiscal 2026, with the state adding $0.1120 and Park and Planning adding $0.2940. Unpaid taxes can lead to a lien sold at the annual tax sale on the second Monday in May.

The county caps the taxable assessment increase for fiscal 2026 at 3%, while the state cap is 10% after the first full tax year. The county's Homeowner Protection Program may keep a limited-income home out of tax sale for at least three years, though enrollment is limited.

If the house you are selling has unpaid taxes, pay the balance from the closing proceeds, or ask the Treasury for a payoff before the May sale date.

Before and after closing

Sort the paperwork before the closing date. Confirm who pays the county transfer tax, check whether the contract carries the water and sewer or impact fee disclosures, and ask the title company whether it will make the two trips or send a courier. Bring the signed deed, the intake sheet and the Finance Affidavit if an exemption applies, and carry a check made out to The Clerk of the Circuit Court.

After recording, ask for the deed back by mail or pick it up at the counter. The county shows recorded and verified land records online at landrec.msa.maryland.gov, so you can search for your deed later. Clerks cannot give legal advice or run title searches, so questions about the deed's wording belong with your attorney or title company. A cash sale skips the lender's timeline, but the recording steps and taxes are the same.

About the county

Prince George's County borders Washington, D.C. on its west side and had 967,201 residents in the 2020 census, making it the second-most populous county in Maryland. Upper Marlboro is the county seat, and Bowie is the largest city. Large unincorporated communities include Largo, Clinton, Oxon Hill, Fort Washington and National Harbor. Metro, MARC and the nearby airports make the county easy to reach, which helps showings.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Prince George's County land records office?

The Land Records Division is in the Judiciary Administrative Services Building at 14701 Governor Oden Bowie Drive, Room J1108, in Upper Marlboro. It is open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.

Do I pay the county first or the court first?

The county Office of Finance in Largo comes first, then the Land Records Division in Upper Marlboro. Call 301-952-4030 for the Finance step.

What is the Prince George's County transfer tax rate?

It is 1.4% under County Code 10-187 and 10-188. The state also charges a 0.5% transfer tax and a recordation tax of $5.50 per $1,000.

Can I search Prince George's County land records online?

Yes. Use the Land Records Online Search at landrec.msa.maryland.gov, which shows recorded and verified land records volumes. Clerks cannot give legal advice or run title searches.

What does it cost to record a deed?

An instrument of 1 to 9 pages is $20, covering every page for a principal residence, plus a $40 surcharge on recorded documents. Call 301-780-2253 to confirm the current amount before you record.
